claims.text: Simultaneous wear and corrosion resistance in high-entropy alloys is governed by rapid, self-regenerating formation of a multicomponent adherent oxide film.
Reactive alloying elements such as Cr and Mo form the proposed passive film.
The passive film continuously repairs itself during wear exposure.
The regenerated passive film protects the underlying alloy from both mechanical removal and corrosive attack.
The proposed initial material is a homogenized equiatomic high-entropy alloy containing, for example, Cr, Co, Fe, Ni, and Mo.
Arc melting followed by homogenization heat treatment produces a uniform microstructure and chemical distribution.
The controlled intervention combines sliding wear with immersion in 3.5 wt% NaCl under a fixed load and sliding speed.
The proposed structural mediator is a thin, adherent, multicomponent oxide film that regenerates during wear cycles.
Mechanical wear exposes fresh reactive alloy surfaces.
Freshly exposed reactive surfaces rapidly oxidize in the corrosive environment.
The alloy's multielement composition favors formation of a protective oxide layer containing several passivating species.
The protective oxide film resists subsequent mechanical removal.
The protective oxide film impedes corrosive dissolution.
The proposed alloy will have lower wear-volume loss than a baseline depleted in key passivating elements.
The proposed alloy will have lower corrosion-current density than the baseline.
The proposed alloy will have a more positive corrosion potential than the baseline.
Reducing or omitting Cr or Mo will produce a less effective protective film in the baseline alloy.
The proposed mechanism should operate under moderate loads in 3.5 wt% NaCl at room temperature.
Extremely high loads, severe tribological conditions, or highly aggressive corrosive environments may overwhelm the oxide film and cause the protective mechanism to fail.
Failure to observe lower wear loss and corrosion-current density, or failure to observe a persistent protective oxide film, relative to the baseline would falsify the hypothesis.
